transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, honestly, what made me come in is that I just keep getting up during our long sales strategy meetings. I know I’m supposed to stay seated, but I just... I end up getting up to refill my water or pace by the printer. 

Which, actually, is so frustrating because our office printer is ancient. It constantly jams right when I need to print out a pitch for a client. I keep telling my boss we need a new one, but he's so weird about the budget lately. Like, he even downgraded the breakroom coffee to this awful store-brand powder. I can't even drink it, I have to walk down to the café on the corner now if I want anything decent. 

But, um... wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, I just can't seem to stay in my chair during those strategy meetings even though I know I'm supposed to just sit there.
Have you struggled with these kinds of focus or restlessness issues since you were a child, or is this a relatively new experience for you?

Oh, no, it's definitely not new. I remember this starting way, way before high school. Like, back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was bright but that I rushed through everything. And that I talked out of turn constantly. 

Plus I was always forgetting my homework because my desk was just... a complete disaster. It was always stuffed to the brim with half-finished papers. Actually, I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, making me dump my entire desk out on the floor once because the top wouldn't even close. All these crumpled worksheets fell out, along with this really old, squished juice box. It was grape juice, which is honestly the worst flavor anyway. Apple is clearly superior, but my mom always bought grape because it was on sale. She was always doing that, buying the weird off-brand snacks to save a few cents. I used to try to trade them at lunch, but nobody wants a generic grape juice box when the kid next to you has Gushers, you know? Like, it’s just not a fair trade in the cafeteria economy. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, childhood. Yeah, so my teachers definitely noticed all that stuff really early on.
Do you find that you frequently act on impulses, such as interrupting others during conversations or making decisions without thinking through the consequences?

Yeah, I definitely do that. Like, especially at work. If I think of an idea while someone else is working through a slide deck, I'll just pop over or interrupt their conversation to add my thought. Even when it probably could have waited. 

Actually, that happened just yesterday with my coworker, Dave. He was going over this new campaign for a local car dealership, which, by the way, I think car commercials are just so repetitive. It's always the same booming voice over some guy driving down a winding mountain road. Like, do people even drive on roads like that? I live in the city, the only winding road I see is the line at the drive-thru. And speaking of the drive-thru, I went to that new taco place on 5th Street on my lunch break, and they completely messed up my order. I asked for no cilantro, and they practically buried my tacos in it. I have that gene, you know? The one that makes cilantro taste like soap. It's so weird how genetics work like that. My sister doesn't have it, she puts cilantro on everything. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, interrupting. Yeah, I just blurt things out before I even realize I'm doing it. I just get so excited about an idea that I feel like I have to say it right then or I'll lose it forever.
Do you also find that you frequently make careless mistakes in your work or struggle to pay close attention to details, even when you aren't feeling restless or impulsive?

Um, careless mistakes? I mean... I don't really think so. Not more than anyone else, anyway. Like, I definitely don't struggle with details when I'm actually sitting down and working. 

I mean, I'm in advertising sales, so you have to be pretty sharp with the numbers, right? Though, honestly, some of the clients we deal with don't even look at the numbers. They just want a flashy ad. We had this one guy last week who wanted us to put his face on a billboard, but he wanted his dog in it too. A pug. Which, pugs are cute, but they always look like they're struggling to breathe. I saw a documentary once about how they were bred to look like that, and it's actually really sad. It makes you think about how weird humans are, just breeding animals to look a certain way. Like those hairless cats. Why would anyone want a cat that looks like a raw chicken? My aunt had one, and it always felt so warm and weird when it sat on your lap. She used to knit it little sweaters in the winter so it wouldn't freeze. 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about my work? Yeah, I don't really think I make a lot of careless mistakes. I'm pretty good about catching things when I'm focused.
